A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ASyMOB by the same authors. Their main text, tables, figures, equations and complete Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on ASyMOB, including Table 2 accuracies, perturbation and code-use experiments, CAS case studies, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on the expanded benchmark, including model and SymPy results, a contamination experiment, and topic-level and statistical analyses.

M1.justification: The seed-perturbation generation framework and answer-validation pipeline remain unchanged: regex extraction, SymPy parsing with Gemini fallback, and symbolic or numerical verification. The detailed validation rules in v2 Section 2.2 already appeared in v1 Appendix B. Added parameter settings and diagnostic experiments do not establish a new benchmark algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions already evaluate integrals, limits, differential equations, series and hypergeometrics; hypergeometrics appears in v1 Figure 7. v2 adds the all-ones Numeric-All-0 input condition and evaluation with the original seed question and answer supplied in context. These extend test scenarios within the retained mathematical domains.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds a full-benchmark SymPy baseline, extending CAS comparison beyond v1's case studies. It also adds code-enabled GPT-4o alongside its no-code evaluation and replaces Gemma-3-27b-it with Gemma-3n-e4b-it. These materially revise the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: The evaluation expands from 61 seeds and 17,092 questions to 100 seeds and 35,368 questions. Numeric-All includes the new zero-digit condition, and the variance subset expands from 50 two-digit variants per seed to 50 each at two and three digits. Section 4 adds seed-answer prompting experiments, and Figure 1 revises the reported tool-use prompts. Pass@1 and the existing numerical validation tolerance remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds contamination stress tests, comparisons addressing expression length as an alternative explanation, a robustness-versus-seed-accuracy analysis, topic-stratified analysis, and diagnostics of dependence among generated questions. These substantially broaden the questions investigated. The hybrid LLM–CAS case study is retained as Figure 7, previously Figure 6.

E5.justification: Figures 2–3 newly report Wald 95% confidence intervals. Appendix C.3 adds seed-clustered residual uncertainty, effective sample-size estimation, residual correlations and split-half checks. This substantially extends v1's variance summaries. The additional random coefficient variants are distinct questions, not evidence of repeated runs on identical prompts.

E6.justification: Results are extensively revised under the expanded benchmark. Table 2 reports DeepSeek-R1 at 44.5% overall in v1 and 78.3% in v2, joining the leading group. GPT-4.1's code/no-code totals change from 23.6/19.8 to 46.2/48.9, reversing its reported code advantage. v2 adds SymPy's 39.2% total and contamination and topic-level outcomes. These are results under changed conditions, not controlled cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix C.3 introduces a substantial mathematical construction absent from v1: Jeffreys-smoothed leave-one-out difficulty estimates, calibrated logistic probabilities, residuals, a seed-clustered standard-error estimator with finite-cluster correction, and an IID-equivalent sample-size definition. The perturbation identities themselves are retained; no new theorem proving LLM reasoning ability is supplied.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a diagnostic symbolic-math benchmark, perturbation sensitivity, stronger-model robustness and hybrid tool-use benefits. v2 explicitly claims previously unexplored symbolic and equivalence perturbation categories and broadens the leading robustness group to include DeepSeek-R1. These refine novelty and claim scope without replacing the main thesis.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation and qualifications: equivalence variants are framed as diagnostic stress tests rather than representative problem distributions; input length is examined as an explanation; SymPy-favoring selection bias and dependence among variants are acknowledged. It also distinguishes seed-answer contamination from training on perturbation procedures and offers new explanations for frontier models' limited benefit from tools.

D1.justification: Appendix B replaces provider-level expenditure totals with per-model/setup costs and newly specifies exclusion of answers that fail both parsing routes, without establishing that exclusion handling changed. However, v1's temperature settings and named API intermediaries disappear. Code/data access links and the detailed numerical validation parameters were already available in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds explicit positioning against neuro-symbolic data generation and a sharper novelty contrast with GSM-Symbolic. It adds discussion or citations involving PAL, AFlow, MathArena, RIMO and PutnamBench, while removing Omni-MATH. The existing positioning around university-level symbolic manipulation versus word problems remains central; publication and bibliography-format updates alone are not substantive additions.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the introduction, methodology, results and discussion are rewritten. Validation details move from Appendix B into the main text, benchmark-error examples move into Appendix A.2, and Appendix C gains a structured sequence of analyses. This constitutes extensive narrative revision and reorganization.

P2.justification: The main text changes to a two-column layout, Figure 1 becomes vertically arranged, and Figures 2–3 are redrawn with error bars and revised legends. v2 adds a robustness scatterplot and cost/topic tables, converts the identity list into Table 3, and expands the heatmaps. The existing hybrid case is relocated and renumbered; variance-heatmap success/failure markers are removed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence supporting the benchmark's diagnostic claims. The systematic SymPy comparison, contamination and length checks, topic analysis, and treatment of seed dependence address important comparison and validity questions largely unexamined in v1. These gains outweigh the loss of temperature/provider details and the unreconciled v1 subgroup figures retained in Appendix A.3. The improvement comes from stronger scrutiny and qualification of the benchmark, not simply its increased size or changed scores.
